content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3: overtime backfill for the General sick wave, predicted 84.6% service level for 11:45-15:30 at ₹6,870 extra.","why":"General has 9 sick absences against about 2.4 on a usual day, leaving 16 agents on the phones against 20 planned since 08:30. Calls are not the problem: they are 15% below forecast and handle time is normal. Doing nothing is predicted to drop the disruption window to 77.3%, with General at 69.8%. P3 offers overtime to General agents across 12:15-16:00 and to 4 Payments agents 15:00-16:00. It also delays breaks, moves 2 cross-skilled agents to General 13:00-14:00 and cancels General coaching 15:00-16:30. This lifts both queues to about 84-85% (General 84.9%, Payments 84.4%) and cuts abandons to 3.3%. It is the only option that reaches the 80% target, it breaks no policy rules, and the rest of the day rises to 90.7%.","trade_offs":["Cost: P3 adds ₹6,870. P2 costs ₹2,016 but just misses target at 79.7%, and General would sit at 74.5%. P0 and P1 cost nothing but miss badly at 77.3% and 73.2%.","Customer impact: P3 has the lowest predicted abandon rate at 3.3%. The others range from 4.6% (P2) to 6.2% (P1). P1 is worse than doing nothing.","Risk to Payments: moving 2 agents to General is offset by Payments overtime, so Payments holds at 84.4%. Under P1, without backfill, Payments drops to 77.3%.","P3 depends on enough agents accepting the overtime offers. If uptake is low, results will fall short."],"watch":"Track overtime acceptances early, especially the 8 General slots for 14:15-16:00. Also watch Payments, which has 7 sick absences against a usual 2.6, so the illness may be spreading. Further absences there could pull Payments below target, particularly while its 2 cross-skilled agents are on General."}
